commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[tests] Make misleading tests check what their names claim (#10883)

Fix the twelve tests an audit flagged as not checking what their names
or docstrings claim, so each one now fails when the behavior it names
breaks. Two of the fixed tests expose real product bugs. Those are
marked as expected failures with `xfail(strict=True)`, so CI fails as
soon as someone fixes the bug and forgets to remove the mark.

The audit found tests that passed no matter what the code did. The olmo2
sequence-length test compared the model with itself because both inputs
were the same 128 tokens. The mistral backward test ran under
`filter_eval_shape`, so it never computed a gradient. The LoRA
checkpoint test saved a checkpoint and never loaded it back. Others
asserted only private state, swallowed `NotImplementedError`, had their
only assertion commented out, or avoided the colliding key they claimed
to test. Each test now checks its named behavior through observable
results. The llama, mistral, and olmo2 backward tests share a new
`assert_grads_finite_and_nonzero` helper in `levanter.testing.helpers`,
which requires every floating-point gradient leaf to be finite and not
all zero.

Three items needed a judgment call. The cache API no longer has shard
groups, so the "with groups" cache test now splits each shard into
several processor batches with a short last batch, and is renamed to say
so. The async unknown-file-type cache test was a copy of the sync test,
and the cache build has no async path, so it is deleted. The olmo2
sequence-length test now matches its llama and olmo3 siblings: four
layers instead of the default 32, and their `1e-5` tolerance instead of
`1e-6`. The old `1e-6` only ever compared a computation with itself;
across a 64-token prefix and the full sequence, float32 accumulation
order alone moves logits by up to 6e-6 at four layers.

The two expected failures are product bugs. First, Zephyr worker
counters are keyed by name only (`_InProcessWorkerContext._counters`,
and `CounterSnapshot.counters` is a name-keyed dict). A stage counter
that shares a name with a pipeline counter merges into the pipeline
entry, so `pipeline.update_counter("metric", 1)` followed by
`stage("stg").update_counter("metric", 2)` reads 3 from pipeline scope
and nothing from the stage. The coordinator already keys completed
totals by stage and name, so the gap is on the worker side. Second,
NamedRef cannot read through a Python list index. The list goes straight
to `jax.Ref` indexing, which treats it as several indices and raises
`ValueError: too many values to unpack`, even for `base_ref[{"x": [2,
4]}]`. `slice()` accepts list prefixes, so the list cases moved into
their own expected-failure test and the other index kinds still pass.

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
[marina] Add the Belay app with public pages and a session queue (#10829)

Add the Marin Belay app to Marina. It is the shared home for Belay's
idea queue and results: anyone can read the project page, the Status
checklist and the Hero MFU page; maintainers approve ideas and set run
limits from an admin view; and Belay agent sessions claim work and
report through it. Until now this ran from a maintainer's laptop.

Flow of one idea:

1. A contributor posts an idea on #9514, optionally naming a track
(default: the 8-minute d512 speedrun on the current recipe).
2. A maintainer approves it in the admin view. The view loads #9514 live
and shows the exact stripped text that will be stored: hidden HTML and
invisible characters are removed and flagged. Approve freezes that text
and queues one event. It can also grant a node budget, study hours and a
higher Iris priority than the track's batch default. GitHub reactions do
not approve anything.
3. A Loom `belay` session (#10824) claims the queued events and follows
`experiments/belay/RUNBOOK.md` on `marin_belay_v1_recipe`: register an
`X####` id, add code behind an off-by-default flag if needed, and launch
on Iris against a same-commit control. It replies once on the idea's
#9514 comment.
4. The same session waits on short runs, records results in the
registry, and writes the idea's thread in this app. It edits the #9514
reply to the verdict. Runs that outlast the session are picked up when
due.
5. Wins are escalated; only a maintainer adopts a change into the
recipe.

Infrastructure:

| Piece | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| This app | Marina, unnamed applet
`33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15`, public mode | Ideas, queue,
sessions, threads, activity, settings; public pages and data |
| Public pages |
`https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/`
| Read-only, no sign-in. Views are fragments (`#status`,
`#status/X####`, `#mfu`), because Marina serves an applet only at its
root. Transcripts, escalation notes, job ids and identities are omitted
|
| Admin and session API |
`https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15/`
(IAP) | Admin routes require a listed approver. `/api/agent/claim`
accepts Loom's VM service account or an approver. Every later session
write needs the per-session secret `claim` issued, and is refused once
the session has finished |
| Sessions | Loom `belay` profile, one at a time, started by a 10-minute
watch (#10824) | Do all the work through `uv run python -m
experiments.belay <command>` |
| Runs | Iris; H100 tracks on cw-us-east-02a | At the track's band
(batch) unless an approval granted more, within the node cap or the
idea's grant |
| Records | `marin_belay_v1_registry` branch, public W&B `marin_moe` |
Permanent results and analysis reports; #9514 gets one reply per idea |

A #9514 comment the registry already lists is never queued again; only a
maintainer re-queue with a note reruns it. Session reports cannot set
node, hours or priority grants, and a retried report changes nothing.
Page assets carry a frontend digest, so a cached script never pairs with
newer data. Public markdown renders with raw HTML disabled and only
http(s) links.

A private preview of this branch, seeded with demo data and with
dispatch off, is at
https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/b5a0d602-3171-47ae-a9f0-7ed1214038cd/
(Marina sign-in). It will be archived after merge.

First release, by someone with release rights: `uv run marina release
infra/marina/apps/belay --id 33801d46-e280-46f9-b994-2c78603cdf15
--base-version 0 --mode public`. Then check the approvers in the admin
settings and keep dispatch off until #10824's watch is enabled. Marina
is shared: any user with release rights can republish this applet or
write its schema, so the allowlists guard the HTTP routes, not the data.

Part of #9451

commits.message:
[iac] Scope the Marin Belay CoreWeave user to its data and run prefixes (#10833)

Add a CoreWeave organization access policy for Marin Belay's dedicated
user (`coreweave/unAfPLe6TaiRmJsewaUog`), so Belay runs can read their
data and write only their own outputs.

Since #10475 every CoreWeave job carries its submitter's storage keys,
so the key Belay's Loom sessions submit with is exactly what every Belay
job, including agent-written code, can reach. A request must pass both
the bucket policy, which admits every principal in the organization, and
an organization access policy. The Belay user is in no groups, so this
policy is its only grant:

| Access | Paths |
|---|---|
| List | `marin-us-east-02a`, `marin-us-east-08a` |
| Read | `marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/hero_tok/*`, `marin/paloma/*`,
`marin/uncheatable_eval/*`; `marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=30d/xprof/*` |
| Read, write, delete | `marin-us-east-02a/marin/tmp/ttl=30d/belay/*`
and its Levanter temp-checkpoint path under
`tmp/ttl=14d/checkpoints-temp/` |

Everything else, including hero checkpoints and other runs, is denied by
default. The read paths are every storage path in a real Belay
speedrun's config (`belay-X0221-control-b`); if the tokenizer turns out
to load from elsewhere, the first run's error names the path to add. The
tests check representative allowed and denied paths, including a hero
checkpoint.

Applying this needs a CoreWeave console API token, like the existing
bucket policies. Preview it before applying, since the console's policy
validator is the authority on the resource syntax. The key for this user
is created in the console and stored as
`BELAY_CW_KEY_ID`/`BELAY_CW_KEY_SECRET` for the Loom profile in #10824.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[dedup] Retire legacy exact dedup, including paragraph-level (#10886)

Remove the old exact-dedup module
(`marin.processing.classification.deduplication.exact`) entirely.
Whole-document exact dedup already lives in datakit's
`global_exact_deduplicate`, and paragraph-level dedup is retired, as
agreed in [review
discussion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10886#issuecomment-6619134507).

The module offered two modes. The document mode had no callers once
datakit took over production exact dedup. The paragraph mode cut
repeated lines out of later documents and was used only by two tests.
Datakit has no paragraph equivalent, and reviewers preferred removing
the feature to porting it; it can come back if needed.

Deleting it also removes `dedup_commons.py`: its only other user,
`fuzzy_dups`, needed just a parquet batch reader, and now uses zephyr's
`iter_parquet_row_groups` instead.

Consolidate's `remove_spans` filter stays as a general span-removal
filter. `test_consolidate` now writes the span attribute file by hand
instead of running dedup to produce it, and still checks that the first
copy is unchanged, later copies lose the attributed text, and unique
documents are intact. The test now writes its input shards sorted by id,
because consolidate merge-joins input and attributes on sorted ids; the
shared fixture's unsorted shard had silently skipped one attributed
document.

The integration pipeline now drops exact-duplicate documents instead of
cutting out duplicate paragraphs. It runs `global_exact_deduplicate` on
the normalized output and feeds a `remove_docs` filter on its `dup_doc`
attribute into the cleaned step. This is valid because normalize sets
each record ID to a hash of its text, so equal IDs mean identical
documents.

Follows up #10880.

commits.message:
[data] Declare Smartie campaign release cohorts in the catalog (#10891)

The RL Data Atlas reads only the published curation catalog, and none of
the Snowball Smartie campaign's published cohorts appear there. This
declares the five release cohorts as inventory-only sources, each pinned
to an exact Hugging Face revision: CalibForge admitted (2,205), repaired
CalibForge shared v2 (324), SWE-Smith admitted (8,045), and staged
SWE-Smith Stage 1 (1,699) and Stage 3 (778). Campaign admission, splits
and qualification evidence already live in each release, so the entries
are pointers; a conversion recipe would invent a second provenance.
Notes carry each release's own admission facts: the admitted entries
state their oracle evidence, the CalibForge admitted entry records its
manifest's not-published status and points to the shared v2 release as
usable, and the staged archives carry the qualification-is-not-admission
warning and the host-local Docker image limitation.

Publishing these rows requires a catalog campaign, which the driver fix
unblocks. Iris authorizes an elevated worker container profile only when
the launching parent task carries the same profile; the coordinator job
the driver created carried none, so the coordinator's worker launch
failed the admin-only `set_container_profile` check. Coordinator
resources now propagate the worker profile end to end.

commits.message:
[rl] Align selected-token scores with compact Megatron logits (#10592)

Megatron removes masked padding before its forward pass. Map
teacher-selected response tokens through that compacted layout before
computing their log probabilities; slicing by the original padded
response width can select the wrong positions or fail on short
responses.

CPU regressions compare selected-token values and gradients with an
independent padded reference across unequal prompt and response lengths.
Tensor-parallel selected-ID scoring remains unsupported by this path.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[levanter] Use a 4096 vocab block for the CE backward on AMD GPUs (#10341)

On AMD Instinct GPUs, run the cross-entropy backward with vocab blocks
of at least 4096 instead of 1024 when the vocab has at least 65536
entries. That reduces June Snowball step time by 0.7% to 2.1%, depending
on the setup.

The batched_xla cross-entropy kernel splits the vocabulary into blocks.
The backward pass used the same block size as the autotuned forward,
which picks 1024 on MI350X. With June's 128256-token vocab, that is 126
blocks. Each block adds its share of the input gradient into a float32
[B, H] accumulator (B tokens, H hidden size), so every block reads and
writes the whole accumulator once. On MI350X those passes cost 34 ms per
June Snowball step. With 4096-wide blocks there are 32 passes instead of
126.

The forward pass and its autotuning are unchanged, and NVIDIA GPUs keep
their current block sizes.

On a one-GPU MI350X stand-in for one EP8 rank of June Snowball, step
time goes from 2.414 to 2.363 s (-2.1%). On 8-GPU MI355X nodes, batch
128 per node, this change alone gives:

| Nodes | PGLE | Before (s/step) | After (s/step) | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | no | 2.531 | 2.479 | -2.0% |
| 1 | yes | 2.392 | 2.362 | -1.3% |
| 2 | no | 3.286 | 3.234 | -1.6% |
| 2 | yes | 3.109 | 3.087 | -0.7% |

Combined with the ring_dedup slot-weight gradient gather (#10343), batch
128 per node, with PGLE:

| Setup | Before (s/step) | After (s/step) | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One 8x MI350X node | 2.906 | 2.805 | -3.5% |
| One 8x MI355X node | 2.523 | 2.448 | -3.0% |
| Two 8x MI355X nodes (EP8 x DP2, batch 256) | 3.198 | 3.106 | -2.9% |

Larger blocks round slightly more. Each block's input-gradient matmul
returns bfloat16 before it is added to the float32 accumulator, so a
4096-wide block rounds a partial sum over 4x more vocab entries. At the
June lm-head shape (8192 tokens, H=2560, V=128256) on MI350X, the
relative L2 error of the input gradient against a float32 reference is
1.75e-3 with 4096-wide blocks and 1.68e-3 with 1024-wide blocks. The
weight gradient's error is 8.95e-4 in both cases.

Three CE kernel tests fail on MI350X, and they fail on main as well.

Part of #9812.

Co-authored-by: Amy Sartran <users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[iris/grug] Save completed steps on preemption (#10774)

Grug training ranks now agree on the completed step after SIGTERM and
commit that step's model, optimizer, and data-position checkpoint before
exiting. A pending asynchronous save completes first; background pruning
does not delay shutdown. The `moe_pipeline` and `moe_hero_pipeline`
entry points use the same stop decision, while `recovery` writes its
final local snapshot. A preempted trainer exits with SIGTERM status
after the save so Iris can retry instead of recording partial training
as complete.

The shutdown budget is a typed `termination_grace` duration on
`IrisClient.submit` and Fray's `JobRequest`, with `--termination-grace`
on `iris job run`. The controller resolves a 10-second default,
validates the 1-110-second range, and persists the duration through
retries and federation. Grug explicitly requests 60 seconds. The
supervisor receives that budget; workers and Pods permit five additional
seconds for teardown. Container discovery preserves the budget when a
worker adopts a running task. Iris generates the supervisor's internal
metadata; application environment variables cannot set the
infrastructure budget.

At `6279f37`, a [two-H100 Grug base
probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10774#issuecomment-6501275454)
ran separate preemption trials during a step and during a pending async
save. Both committed step 3, restored the model, optimizer, and example
position, and matched uninterrupted step-6 state and batch hashes under
deterministic GPU settings. Supervisor exit took 8.75 seconds during a
step and 10.22 seconds during the async save; a stalled commit was
force-killed after 61.12 seconds. The probe used about 0.94 MiB of
checkpoint state. Production-size timing, automatic Iris retry, and live
worker/Pod shutdown remain unvalidated; workers/controllers were not
redeployed.

Part of #10761

[grug] Keep hero permanent checkpoints every 500 steps over the final 5000 (#10896)

Keep a permanent hero checkpoint every 500 steps over the final 5000
steps of the 390251-step run (385500 through 390000, plus the final step
390251), instead of every 6000. That gives a dense series of end-of-run
checkpoints for analysis and averaging.

The keep policy gains one range: the 6000 cadence holds through step
385251 (`num_steps − 5000`), and every 500 steps after that. Earlier
ranges, including the pinned 55000, are unchanged. The test checks the
kept steps with Levanter's own interval lookup: 48000, 54000, 55000,
60000 near the pin, and 378000, 384000, then 385500…390000.

Cost: about 9 more permanent checkpoints than the 6000 cadence (384000
and 390000 were already kept), at several TB each, under the
delete-protected `marin/grug/hero-*` prefix. Check storage headroom
before deploying.

Deploying: the running hero (`hero-ctx65k-step372k`, at step 382505 on
2026-11-04) picks up a new keep policy only on relaunch with the same
run id from its newest checkpoint. Training is unchanged. 385500 is
about 3000 steps (13 hours) away, so the relaunch has to land before
then for the first dense checkpoint to be kept.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[evals] Curate Evalchemy benchmarks as canonical tasks (#10757)

Curate Evalchemy benchmarks as canonical TaskSpec rows tagged `eval`,
with pinned
source inputs and typed execution and summary metadata. The catalog
contains 96
declarations for 31 benchmark names, including subject and protocol
variants.
Publication retains source order, duplicate positions and the full
source
population. Default training curation excludes evaluation sources.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  E["Experiment: acquire pinned source; bind EvalDataset recipe + protocol"] --> C["TaskCompendium: convert, publish"]
  C --> T["TaskSpec Parquet: context, grader, resources, tags, labels"]
  C --> P["Protocol + per-row operation inputs + immutable manifest"]
  T --> D["Marin evaluation application: select cohorts, expand trials, resume"]
  P --> D
  CLI["Experiment entrypoint: endpoint, tokenizer, secrets, privileged Iris CPU worker"] --> D
  D --> R["RolloutEngine: one generation attempt or likelihood transport"]
  R --> M["Model endpoint"]
  R -->|generation grading| G["Verifyit + source graders; executable graders through Shellbox"]
  G --> B["Bubblewrap grading machines"]
  R --> D
  D --> F["FineStore: individual results, attempts, selection ledger, evidence"]
  F -.-> X["Evaldash raw import and summary computation: separate migration"]
```

| Code | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/evalchemy/` | Source
pins, environments, sampling, trials and dataset-specific cohort/budget
declarations |
| `taskcompendium.importers.evalchemy` | Reusable source conversion,
prompts and source grading programs |
| `taskcompendium.evaluation` | Protocol/item schema, verified corpus
reader and generic selection |
| `marin.rollouts.evaluation` | Mixed-corpus scheduling, raw FineStore
persistence and retry/resume |
| `experiments.evaluation.task_driver` | CLI and deployment bindings |
| `rolloutengine`, `verifyit`, `shellbox` | Attempt/model
infrastructure, shared grading, and machine isolation |

TaskSpec owns the canonical prompt and grader. Its tags and
string-valued labels
are projected into normalized Parquet for queries without decoding task
payloads.
Protocols describe ordered label/tag groups and token budgets: MRCR
declares its
bin/needle cohorts in experiments, and GraphWalks declares a
reference-dependent
output budget. The generic selector contains no dataset dispatch.
Sidecars hold
additional inputs such as likelihood continuations and prompt variants.

For example, curate MATH500 through its registered recipe:

```bash
CURATION_REPORT_ROOT="s3://YOUR_BUCKET/eval-curation/math500"
uv run --package marin-core --group test python \
  -m experiments.post_training.task_curation.driver \
  --mode quick --source evalchemy-math500 \
  --output-root "$CURATION_REPORT_ROOT" --run
```

Curation downloads the pinned source, converts all 500 rows, and
publishes the
TaskSpec shards, operation sidecars, protocol and completion manifest.
Set
`CORPUS_ROOT` to `sources[0].path` in
`$CURATION_REPORT_ROOT/campaign.json`.
Start a model server separately and put its OpenAI-compatible base URL
in
`endpoint.txt`; supply its credential through `OPENAI_API_KEY`. With an

[`EvaluationRunConfig`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/evals-as-data-migration/docs/references/evaluation-tasks.md#curate-and-run)
that
records the served model, tokenizer, context window and token budget:

```bash
CORPUS_ROOT="s3://YOUR_BUCKET/COMPLETED_CORPUS_PATH"
RESULT_ROOT="s3://YOUR_BUCKET/eval-results/math500-run-1"
uv run --package marin-core --group test python \
  -m experiments.evaluation.task_driver \
  --dataset "$CORPUS_ROOT" --config run-config.json \
  --endpoint-file endpoint.txt --cluster cw-us-east-02a \
  --output "$RESULT_ROOT"
```

Remote corpus and result roots must be shared storage near the selected
cluster.
The default worker is a privileged Iris CPU container using Shellbox
bubblewrap,
with concurrency 64. Repeat `--dataset` to include multiple corpora, and
repeat
the command with the same `--output` root to resume. Completed grades,
including zeros, remain recorded. Infrastructure errors retry without
becoming
incorrect grades. A verifier or judge failure after a complete model
response
reuses that response; a model request failure sends a new request. The
run config
records endpoint options such as `skip_special_tokens: false`, which
retains the
`<|end_think|>` boundary that NUPA uses to exclude reasoning from
answers when
Grug or Snowball has no reasoning parser. Resume rejects mismatched
corpus or
protocol hashes, execution revision, run settings, or solver, tokenizer
and
judge identities. Credentials stay outside persisted metadata.

The driver writes raw observations; dataset summary metadata describes
consumer
reductions. Migrating the legacy Evalchemy launchers and checkpoint
callers,
adding their missing protocol variants, and connecting Evaldash's raw
importer
remain follow-up work before deleting `vendor/evalchemy`. Harbor
migration is
also separate. NUPA scoring follows #10876's extraction rules, and GSM8K
scoring
follows #10808's final-answer rules. Other grader corrections are
tracked in
#10828. The updated TaskSpec and protocol schemas require newly curated
corpora
and result roots.

commits.message:
[echo] Add work-log commands and the echo-log skill (#10756)

Add `work-log recent`, `projects`, `show`, and `add` to the Echo CLI,
and an `echo-log` skill that tells agents to read the work log at the
start of shared work and add one entry per milestone. The commands call
the existing `/work_log` API, so the server records the author and
callers need no database grant.

The API now stores project slugs trimmed and in lowercase, and the
project filter ignores case. Live entries used both `marinskyrl:` and
`MarinSkyRL:` as prefixes for one area; migration `m0003` rewrites
existing rows so they match. `GET /work_log/projects` (MCP
`list_work_log_projects`) lists each slug with its entry count and
latest entry time, over 30 days by default, so an agent can reuse an
existing slug. Slugs with different names, such as
`hero-learner-bottlenecks` and `hero-learner-bottlenecks-01a13c0f`, stay
separate. These server changes take effect at the next Echo release,
which runs the migration.

When Echo refuses a write because of access (no credentials, 401, or
403), `add` prints a warning and exits 0. Other errors still fail the
command. The skill tells an agent to stop using the work log for the
session after the first refusal, and not to retry or debug access.

The closed #7531 had a script that wrote directly to the `context`
database on `marin-metadata`. Echo now serves its work log from Marina's
database, so entries written through that script are not visible to the
team.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[finestore] Retry archive initialization after an in-flight conflict (#10895)

Retry archive marker creation when a conditional write conflicts with
another writer's create that is still in flight. `initialize_archive`
reread the marker once after the conflict and asserted that it existed,
so concurrent `DataStore.open` calls on a new root could fail. #10413
fixed the same race in `write_schema`; both now use one bounded
create-or-read retry.

The race failed
`test_concurrent_writers_publish_every_row_through_conflicts` in [CI on
#10892](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/41749958390/job/126312514990).
The simulated-S3 in-flight test now also covers the archive marker. It
failed on every run before this change and passes after it.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Export and upload Hero checkpoints on CPU (#10890)

Stream native Hero checkpoints to BF16 safetensors on one CPU host and
upload them to checkpoint branches in an existing private Hugging Face
repository. The uploader checks repository visibility before writing.
Read authoritative weights in stored layer chunks and reuse the device
exporter's inference mapping, shard format, and verified resume
receipts. Hub uploads bind each branch to its export, card, license and
tokenizer, then publish a completion marker that pins the verified
weights commit. Both exporters write an explicit BF16 dtype. Memory,
concurrency and mesh settings are recorded separately from artifact
identity, so interrupted exports can resume with lower execution limits
while preserving verified shards.

The CPU reader has a 96 GiB cache budget and a separate 32 GiB budget
shared by both shard writers; the documented worker size is 256 GiB to
allow for decoding and runtime buffers. A CW02 check on step 378000
converted all ordinary weights and one six-layer expert chunk: 55
shards, 70.8 GB, 487.6 seconds, and 95.6 GiB peak RSS with zero GPUs.
Every shard's SHA-256 matched the existing GPU export. The measured
source revision is `2767265c133c37eb5666658e8c0f13d095b3764c`; report
and reproduction harness are retained under
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/exports/mochi/benchmarks/cpu-streaming-20261103/`.
Full-model CPU export time and serving numerical parity remain
unmeasured.

Enable two concurrent writers. In a separate CW check, two writers
reduced mean writer-stage wall time from 210 to 183 seconds across
order-reversed rounds of four 7.25 GB shards, with identical output.
This component measurement excludes source restore and device gathers.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[tpu-inference] Launch multi-host TPU serving within one Iris slice (#10535)

Allow `marin-serve iris` and the evaluation launcher to serve one model
across a multi-host TPU slice. A `v4-32` request now submits four
replicas coscheduled by `tpu-name`, starts a Ray head on rank zero and
workers on the other hosts, and publishes the serving endpoint only from
rank zero. Single-host serving keeps its existing path; multi-host
serving requires the isolated TPU vLLM backend, one serving instance
spanning the host replicas, and streaming weights shared by all hosts.

Ray runs inside the same isolated environment as vLLM. Iris supplies the
GCS, Ray Client, dashboard and dashboard-agent ports; worker ports are
kernel-selected. Ray log deduplication is disabled on every host.
Startup reports the Ray process log on failure, and shutdown stops only
the job's own processes. Explicit multi-host evaluation overrides use
direct serving rather than the single-host request broker; automatic
hardware selection is unchanged.

The [four-host smoke
test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10270#issuecomment-6350331747)
established the launch recipe on v4-32 with
`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` in BF16,
TP16/PP1: generation succeeded and one 5,279-token teacher-forced item
matched the H100 reference at mean absolute logprob difference 0.0153.
That test used the task-local launcher, not this refactoring. The pinned
TPU runtime still needs a job-local v4 attention-tile patch; this PR
does not add that patch or change runtime pins. Full MATH500 parity
using this launcher is follow-up work.

Verify without allocation: `uv run marin-serve iris org/model --tpu
v4-32 --tensor-parallel-size 16 --dry-run` prints four replicas,
`CoschedulingConfig(group_by='tpu-name')`, and the allocated port names.
`host-test-budget uv run --frozen --no-sync pytest tests/inference
tests/evaluation/test_model_config.py
tests/evals/test_inference_proxy.py -q`: 290 passed. Repository
formatting and type checks passed with `./infra/pre-commit.py
--changed-files --fix`.

Part of #10270.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[snowball-tpu] [inference] Adopt the TPU stack with native Snowball layer types (#10854)

## tl;dr 

Previous TPU inference on vLLM didn't handle sliding window / global
attention properly. See
https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/34

This pins merged fork main `2f327d385a90347681a7de86472b4bace6e940b2`,
including the native v4 attention-tile fix.

## Detail

Adopt merged fork-main tpu-inference commit
`2f327d385a90347681a7de86472b4bace6e940b2`, paired with unchanged vLLM
`fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`, and remove the Snowball
reference configurations’ `layer_types` overrides. The fork includes the
native layer-schedule fix from [tpu-inference
#34](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/34) and the
v4 attention-tile fix from
[#35](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/35).

The TPU plugin registers its own GrugMoE config. Without native layer
types, vLLM applies the 2048-token cache window to global layers too.
The fixed config derives the training schedule, leaving seven of
Snowball’s 26 layers global. The config registration and JAX model
windowing are unchanged.

The earlier `509d688fa` / `fb02daf` pair served Step12 BF16 on v6e-8 TP8
without `--hf-overrides` in `/karan/rsi244-patched-v6e8`. The backend
trace showed seven unwindowed global layers, 19 local layers at 2048,
and four KV cache groups. Across ten teacher-forced inputs and 35,801
scored tokens, pooled mean absolute logprob difference from the eager
H100 oracle was 0.01598, with 0.0119–0.0182 in every position bin and
0.846% top-1 disagreement. Per-token results matched the earlier
schedule-override control exactly. [Verification and artifact
paths](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/34).

The separate full MATH500 override experiment improved Step12 TPU
accuracy from 0.878/0.882 to 0.940, against H100 0.944; it is supporting
evidence for the schedule correction, not a full MATH500 run on this
commit. The merged v4 tile fix passed 283/283 kernel tests on actual v4,
with 84 exact Step12 tile-selector matches to the previous job-local
patch. The post-merge v6e regression passed 67/67 tests on actual TPU
hardware; the earlier schedule qualification is supporting evidence
rather than a new end-to-end Marin run on this pin.

The earlier pin `509d688fa` was a branch, not fork main. Besides the
[#35](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/35) kernel
change, fork main differs from it in eight source files: MoE routing
(`fused_moe_gmm.py`, `interface/moe.py`), weight cleanup
(`cleanup_sharding.py`), fp8 and unquantized weight handling,
`models/jax/grugmoe.py`, `attention_interface.py` and
`kv_cache_manager.py`. The logprob check and MATH500 results above ran
on older code, not on this pin. No Step12 serving run has used this pin
yet; only the kernel tests have.

Replaces #10606, which GitHub marked merged into its old stack base
during a restack; that merge never reached `main`. This PR targets
`main` directly. Stack order: this PR, then #10535 (multi-host TPU
launcher), then #10607 (H100 vs v4-32 score check), then #10860 (nightly
score check).

Refs #10270 and #10250.

[skyrl] Keep offloaded optimizer moments on CPU during restore (#10480)

Load CPU-offloaded optimizer moments through the CPU parameter mappings.
MCore's existing restore hook leaves FP32 parameter shards on CUDA while
PyTorch loads their state, which temporarily moves the offloaded moments
onto CUDA. After loading, restore the public parameter references and
rebuild the sub-optimizers around the loaded checkpoint state.

The GPU regression checks peak CUDA allocation and exact continuation
after restore for FP32 and BF16 parameters. It has not been run locally;
GPU validation remains pending. Mechanical lint passed; the
affected-test selector delegates these files to the SkyRL CI suite.

The experiment-specific checkpoint schedules, FP32 exports, and
diagnostics are preserved in the [OPD source
snapshot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/694d45bf6fddf0c9d4cb1d01049f06ec7e8853fd)
and the local replay bundle at
`/Users/benfeuer/Documents/experiments/active/opd-sft-proper-controls/artifacts/pr-slimdown/20261031T004421Z/repro/`.

commits.message:
[loom] Fix macOS activation and previews of an unchanged Loom commit (#10889)

* fix two failures from the 2026-11-03 `marin-loom` rollout of Loom
`3764ca10`
* `activate.sh` no longer needs GNU `timeout` on the operator host;
macOS doesn't ship it, so activation exited 127 before it reached the
VM, after Pulumi had already written the new image to VM metadata
* the VM bounds the startup-script restart with its own `timeout`;
`gcloud` bounds SSH key propagation at 60s, and
`ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` drop a connection that stops
responding
* preview no longer raises in `_validated_image_reference` when the Loom
commit is unchanged [^1]
* in a preview, the bare `:latest` ref becomes `pulumi.UNKNOWN`, so the
VM image shows as unknown; `up` still requires the pushed digest
* regression test for the preview failure; a preview of `marin-loom`
from this branch completes and plans the image rebuild, the VM metadata
update, and the activation [^2]

[^1]: `pull=True` makes docker-build rebuild the image on every update.
When preview skips that build and no image input changed, the provider
reports the bare tag as the ref. Every `pulumi up` previews first, so a
rollout of marin-only configuration failed.
[^2]: CI does not select `infra/loom/tests`, because
`infra/ci/select_tests.py` has no source root for `infra/loom`. All 39
tests pass locally.
